retrieved.heading: Duplicate job checks
retrieved.text:
Duplicate scheduled jobs / Duplicate job checks
Check the scheduler lease owner and the idempotency key on each duplicate Northstar job. The scheduler lease duration is 90 seconds; two active lease owners indicate a lease coordination fault.

Consumers must store the job idempotency key before applying a side effect. Replaying a job without a recorded key risks duplicate work; ask the job owner to reconcile the synthetic job IDs.

retrieved.title: API latency investigation
retrieved.heading: Latency checks
retrieved.text:
API latency investigation / Latency checks
Compare Northstar API p50, p95 and p99 latency over the same five-minute window. Split latency by route and release revision. A high p95 with stable p50 suggests a subset of slow requests rather than universal failure.

Inspect database query duration, pool wait time and outbound dependency spans. Compare error rate with latency so that fast failures do not look healthy. Use synthetic trace IDs and never include customer request bodies in screenshots.

A synthetic trace is api=900ms db_wait=650ms query=40ms. This points first to connection pool waiting. Follow the database connection exhaustion runbook and validate the explanation against several traces before changing capacity.

Include the next scheduled update time and all unresolved questions. Label hypotheses explicitly and link the runbook section and version; do not convert an untested hypothesis into a confirmed root cause.

Database deadlock investigation / Deadlock checks
For a Northstar database deadlock, collect the deadlock log with transaction IDs and the lock wait graph. Two transactions updating tables in opposite order can create a circular wait.

Application transactions should acquire locks in a consistent table order and retry aborted transactions with bounded jitter. The database owner must review long transactions before approving query changes.

retrieved.heading: Selector checks
retrieved.text:
Service selector mismatch / Selector checks
Compare the Northstar service selector with pod labels when a service has no endpoints. A label mismatch leaves healthy pods outside the service endpoint set.

Check that the service targetPort matches the application listening port of 8080. Correct a mismatched selector or port through the release manifest review and verify endpoint membership after rollout.

retrieved.title: API authentication after deployment
retrieved.heading: Authentication checks
retrieved.text:
API authentication after deployment / Authentication checks
Check that the deployed Northstar API has AUTH_ISSUER=https://identity.northstar.invalid and AUTH_AUDIENCE=northstar-api. A mismatched issuer or audience causes 401 responses after deployment. Compare the active release configuration with the last healthy release. Never paste bearer tokens into an incident ticket.

Confirm that the gateway forwards the Authorization header. Compare token expiry with the API clock; Northstar permits 30 seconds of clock skew. If only new pods fail, check the mounted identity configuration and restart only after correcting it.

A synthetic log example is auth_failed reason=audience_mismatch release=r42. Record the reason, release and pod name without recording the token. Do not disable authentication to restore service. Escalate to the identity on-call if the issuer endpoint is unavailable.

Compare the Northstar service selector with pod labels when a service has no endpoints. A label mismatch leaves healthy pods outside the service endpoint set.

Check that the service targetPort matches the application listening port of 8080. Correct a mismatched selector or port through the release manifest review and verify endpoint membership after rollout.

retrieved.title: API request rate limiting
retrieved.heading: Rate limit checks
retrieved.text:
API request rate limiting / Rate limit checks
HTTP 429 indicates the Northstar gateway rate limit was exceeded. Inspect the Retry-After response header and use exponential backoff with jitter. The standard tenant budget is 100 requests per minute per tenant.

Check for retry loops and duplicated jobs before requesting a budget increase. Correlate the tenant identifier with gateway counters without recording customer payloads. Clients must respect Retry-After; immediate retries extend the overload.

A synthetic record is rate_limited tenant=demo budget=100 window=60s. If traffic remains within budget but is rejected, send the gateway owner the counter timestamp and request ID. Budget changes require service owner approval and a capacity review.

retrieved.title: Readiness probe flapping
retrieved.heading: Probe checks
retrieved.text:
Readiness probe flapping / Probe checks
For flapping Northstar readiness probes, inspect /ready latency and dependency health in the same window. The probe timeout is two seconds and failureThreshold is three.

Check whether an overloaded database causes probe timeouts. Keep readiness separate from liveness; an unhealthy dependency should remove traffic eligibility without repeatedly killing a healthy process.

retrieved.title: Node memory pressure
retrieved.heading: Node checks
retrieved.text:
Node memory pressure / Node checks
When a Northstar node reports MemoryPressure, compare allocatable memory with scheduled pod requests and node system usage. Pending memory requests and eviction events must be reviewed together.

The platform owner may drain the affected node after confirming spare capacity. Preserve eviction events and verify rescheduled pods become ready; application owners must review inaccurate resource requests.

retrieved.title: Container restart investigation
retrieved.heading: Restart checks
retrieved.text:
Container restart investigation / Restart checks
Inspect the previous container logs and the last termination reason. OOMKilled means the memory limit was exceeded; compare peak memory with the configured limit. Exit code 137 alone is not proof of an application bug.

Check whether the liveness probe fails before startup completes. Northstar worker initialization can take 45 seconds; use the startup probe with a 60-second allowance. Do not increase the liveness frequency during an incident.

A synthetic event is worker-7 OOMKilled limit=512Mi peak=540Mi. Preserve that event and the previous logs. Roll back a new release if memory growth begins with that release. Confirm restart counts stop increasing before closing the incident.

retrieved.title: Pending pod scheduling
retrieved.heading: Scheduling checks
retrieved.text:
Pending pod scheduling / Scheduling checks
Inspect scheduler events for Northstar Pending pods. Insufficient CPU means requested CPU cannot fit on eligible nodes; an unbound persistent volume claim indicates a storage provisioning problem.

Check node selectors, taints and tolerations against the intended node pool. Do not remove isolation labels as a quick fix. Send the exact scheduling reason to the platform or storage owner.

retrieved.title: API authentication after deployment
retrieved.heading: Authentication checks
retrieved.text:
API authentication after deployment / Authentication checks
Check that the deployed Northstar API has AUTH_ISSUER=https://identity.northstar.invalid and AUTH_AUDIENCE=northstar-api. A mismatched issuer or audience causes 401 responses after deployment. Compare the active release configuration with the last healthy release. Never paste bearer tokens into an incident ticket.

Confirm that the gateway forwards the Authorization header. Compare token expiry with the API clock; Northstar permits 30 seconds of clock skew. If only new pods fail, check the mounted identity configuration and restart only after correcting it.

A synthetic log example is auth_failed reason=audience_mismatch release=r42. Record the reason, release and pod name without recording the token. Do not disable authentication to restore service. Escalate to the identity on-call if the issuer endpoint is unavailable.

retrieved.title: Service selector mismatch
retrieved.heading: Selector checks
retrieved.text:
Service selector mismatch / Selector checks
Compare the Northstar service selector with pod labels when a service has no endpoints. A label mismatch leaves healthy pods outside the service endpoint set.

Check that the service targetPort matches the application listening port of 8080. Correct a mismatched selector or port through the release manifest review and verify endpoint membership after rollout.

retrieved.title: API unavailable responses
retrieved.heading: Availability checks
retrieved.text:
API unavailable responses / Availability checks
For HTTP 503, inspect ready endpoints behind the Northstar gateway. If there are no ready pods, check readiness probe events and the dependency health panel. Compare the first failure time with the active release.

The readiness probe uses /ready and must verify the database connection without writing data. A liveness probe must not depend on the database. When the database is down, a database-dependent liveness probe can create a restart storm.

A synthetic gateway log is upstream_unavailable service=api endpoints=0. Capture the endpoint count and rollout status. Restore healthy replicas or roll back the failing release through the approved release procedure; confirm endpoint recovery before declaring success.

retrieved.title: Container image pull failures
retrieved.heading: Image checks
retrieved.text:
Container image pull failures / Image checks
For ImagePullBackOff, inspect the pod events for the exact registry error. A not-found error usually indicates a missing image tag or incorrect repository path. Verify the release manifest points to an immutable digest in the Northstar registry.

For unauthorized errors, check the image pull secret reference and its namespace. Do not display the secret value. Ask the registry owner to rotate expired credentials through the approved secret workflow. Avoid changing the application image to latest.

A synthetic event is FailedPull image=registry.northstar.invalid/api:r42 reason=manifest_unknown. Record the digest expected by the release and the registry owner response. Retry the rollout only after the registry contains the verified artifact.

retrieved.title: Container restart investigation
retrieved.heading: Restart checks
retrieved.text:
Container restart investigation / Restart checks
Inspect the previous container logs and the last termination reason. OOMKilled means the memory limit was exceeded; compare peak memory with the configured limit. Exit code 137 alone is not proof of an application bug.

Check whether the liveness probe fails before startup completes. Northstar worker initialization can take 45 seconds; use the startup probe with a 60-second allowance. Do not increase the liveness frequency during an incident.

A synthetic event is worker-7 OOMKilled limit=512Mi peak=540Mi. Preserve that event and the previous logs. Roll back a new release if memory growth begins with that release. Confirm restart counts stop increasing before closing the incident.

retrieved.title: API authentication after deployment
retrieved.heading: Authentication checks
retrieved.text:
API authentication after deployment / Authentication checks
Check that the deployed Northstar API has AUTH_ISSUER=https://identity.northstar.invalid and AUTH_AUDIENCE=northstar-api. A mismatched issuer or audience causes 401 responses after deployment. Compare the active release configuration with the last healthy release. Never paste bearer tokens into an incident ticket.

Confirm that the gateway forwards the Authorization header. Compare token expiry with the API clock; Northstar permits 30 seconds of clock skew. If only new pods fail, check the mounted identity configuration and restart only after correcting it.

A synthetic log example is auth_failed reason=audience_mismatch release=r42. Record the reason, release and pod name without recording the token. Do not disable authentication to restore service. Escalate to the identity on-call if the issuer endpoint is unavailable.

retrieved.title: Incident escalation and ownership
retrieved.heading: Escalation checks
retrieved.text:
Incident escalation and ownership / Escalation checks
Escalate a customer-facing outage immediately to the Northstar incident commander. For a sustained API error rate above 5 percent over five minutes, declare a severity-two incident. Page the owning service on-call and appoint a scribe.

Record impact, start time, affected services and the latest verified observation. Use the incident channel for updates every fifteen minutes. Route authentication failures to identity, connection exhaustion to database, and failed rollouts to the release on-call.

If the runbooks do not cover the situation, state that the evidence is insufficient and contact the owning on-call. Do not guess a production change. Record the unanswered question so that the owner can add verified guidance after the incident.

retrieved.title: Release rollback procedure
retrieved.heading: Rollback checks
retrieved.text:
Release rollback procedure / Rollback checks
Use the release console to select the last healthy Northstar API revision. Confirm that the database migration is backward compatible before rolling back. If the release removed a column, stop and ask the database on-call for a recovery plan.

Record the current and target release IDs and the incident ID. Shift canary traffic back to the healthy revision, then roll back the remaining replicas through the release console. Require the incident commander to approve a full rollback.

Watch API error rate and p95 latency for ten minutes after rollback. A synthetic recovery record is release=r41 errors=0.2% p95=180ms. Keep the failed revision logs for follow-up and do not rerun destructive migrations.

retrieved.title: Incident escalation and ownership
retrieved.heading: Escalation checks
retrieved.text:
Incident escalation and ownership / Escalation checks
Escalate a customer-facing outage immediately to the Northstar incident commander. For a sustained API error rate above 5 percent over five minutes, declare a severity-two incident. Page the owning service on-call and appoint a scribe.

Record impact, start time, affected services and the latest verified observation. Use the incident channel for updates every fifteen minutes. Route authentication failures to identity, connection exhaustion to database, and failed rollouts to the release on-call.

If the runbooks do not cover the situation, state that the evidence is insufficient and contact the owning on-call. Do not guess a production change. Record the unanswered question so that the owner can add verified guidance after the incident.

retrieved.title: API latency investigation
retrieved.heading: Latency checks
retrieved.text:
API latency investigation / Latency checks
Compare Northstar API p50, p95 and p99 latency over the same five-minute window. Split latency by route and release revision. A high p95 with stable p50 suggests a subset of slow requests rather than universal failure.

Inspect database query duration, pool wait time and outbound dependency spans. Compare error rate with latency so that fast failures do not look healthy. Use synthetic trace IDs and never include customer request bodies in screenshots.

A synthetic trace is api=900ms db_wait=650ms query=40ms. This points first to connection pool waiting. Follow the database connection exhaustion runbook and validate the explanation against several traces before changing capacity.

retrieved.title: Canary release gates
retrieved.heading: Canary gates
retrieved.text:
Canary release gates / Canary gates
Keep the Northstar API canary at 5 percent of traffic for ten minutes. Expand only if its error rate stays below 1 percent and p95 latency stays within 20 percent of the healthy release.

If either canary gate fails, return traffic to the healthy release and ask the release owner to review the new revision. Keep current and target revision IDs in the change record.

retrieved.title: Missing service metrics
retrieved.heading: Metrics checks
retrieved.text:
Missing service metrics / Metrics checks
For missing Northstar metrics, check the scrape target health and the last successful scrape timestamp. The standard scrape interval is 30 seconds; missing samples are not proof of zero traffic.

Verify the exporter route and service discovery labels. If the exporter is healthy but dashboards are empty, compare the dashboard label filter with the actual metric labels before modifying alerts.

retrieved.title: API request rate limiting
retrieved.heading: Rate limit checks
retrieved.text:
API request rate limiting / Rate limit checks
HTTP 429 indicates the Northstar gateway rate limit was exceeded. Inspect the Retry-After response header and use exponential backoff with jitter. The standard tenant budget is 100 requests per minute per tenant.

Check for retry loops and duplicated jobs before requesting a budget increase. Correlate the tenant identifier with gateway counters without recording customer payloads. Clients must respect Retry-After; immediate retries extend the overload.

A synthetic record is rate_limited tenant=demo budget=100 window=60s. If traffic remains within budget but is rejected, send the gateway owner the counter timestamp and request ID. Budget changes require service owner approval and a capacity review.

retrieved.title: Container restart investigation
retrieved.heading: Restart checks
retrieved.text:
Container restart investigation / Restart checks
Inspect the previous container logs and the last termination reason. OOMKilled means the memory limit was exceeded; compare peak memory with the configured limit. Exit code 137 alone is not proof of an application bug.

Check whether the liveness probe fails before startup completes. Northstar worker initialization can take 45 seconds; use the startup probe with a 60-second allowance. Do not increase the liveness frequency during an incident.

A synthetic event is worker-7 OOMKilled limit=512Mi peak=540Mi. Preserve that event and the previous logs. Roll back a new release if memory growth begins with that release. Confirm restart counts stop increasing before closing the incident.

retrieved.title: Database connection exhaustion
retrieved.heading: Pool checks
retrieved.text:
Database connection exhaustion / Pool checks
Check active and idle connections in pg_stat_activity and compare them with max_connections. Northstar API uses a pool maximum of 6 connections per replica. Multiply the pool maximum by the replica count and reserve 20 database connections for operations.

Look for idle-in-transaction sessions and missing connection release paths. Record query age, application name and transaction state. Do not terminate all database sessions; ask the database on-call to review a specific stuck session.

A synthetic alert is pool_wait_ms=5000 api_replicas=12 pool_max=10 db_max=100. This configuration exceeds the connection budget. Reduce application pool demand through an approved release and check that wait time falls. Increasing max_connections requires a separate capacity review.

retrieved.heading: Deadlock checks
retrieved.text:
Database deadlock investigation / Deadlock checks
For a Northstar database deadlock, collect the deadlock log with transaction IDs and the lock wait graph. Two transactions updating tables in opposite order can create a circular wait.

Application transactions should acquire locks in a consistent table order and retry aborted transactions with bounded jitter. The database owner must review long transactions before approving query changes.

Duplicate scheduled jobs / Duplicate job checks
Check the scheduler lease owner and the idempotency key on each duplicate Northstar job. The scheduler lease duration is 90 seconds; two active lease owners indicate a lease coordination fault.

Consumers must store the job idempotency key before applying a side effect. Replaying a job without a recorded key risks duplicate work; ask the job owner to reconcile the synthetic job IDs.

Check node selectors, taints and tolerations against the intended node pool. Do not remove isolation labels as a quick fix. Send the exact scheduling reason to the platform or storage owner.

Container restart investigation / Restart checks
Inspect the previous container logs and the last termination reason. OOMKilled means the memory limit was exceeded; compare peak memory with the configured limit. Exit code 137 alone is not proof of an application bug.

Check whether the liveness probe fails before startup completes. Northstar worker initialization can take 45 seconds; use the startup probe with a 60-second allowance. Do not increase the liveness frequency during an incident.

A synthetic event is worker-7 OOMKilled limit=512Mi peak=540Mi. Preserve that event and the previous logs. Roll back a new release if memory growth begins with that release. Confirm restart counts stop increasing before closing the incident.

retrieved.heading: Rate limit checks

API request rate limiting / Rate limit checks
HTTP 429 indicates the Northstar gateway rate limit was exceeded. Inspect the Retry-After response header and use exponential backoff with jitter. The standard tenant budget is 100 requests per minute per tenant.

Check for retry loops and duplicated jobs before requesting a budget increase. Correlate the tenant identifier with gateway counters without recording customer payloads. Clients must respect Retry-After; immediate retries extend the overload.

A synthetic record is rate_limited tenant=demo budget=100 window=60s. If traffic remains within budget but is rejected, send the gateway owner the counter timestamp and request ID. Budget changes require service owner approval and a capacity review.

Database migration safety / Migration checks
Use expand-and-contract for a Northstar schema change: add compatible fields, deploy dual-compatible consumers, backfill, then remove obsolete fields in a later release. Keep the first release backward compatible.

retrieved.heading: Restart checks
retrieved.text:
Container restart investigation / Restart checks
Inspect the previous container logs and the last termination reason. OOMKilled means the memory limit was exceeded; compare peak memory with the configured limit. Exit code 137 alone is not proof of an application bug.

Check whether the liveness probe fails before startup completes. Northstar worker initialization can take 45 seconds; use the startup probe with a 60-second allowance. Do not increase the liveness frequency during an incident.

A synthetic event is worker-7 OOMKilled limit=512Mi peak=540Mi. Preserve that event and the previous logs. Roll back a new release if memory growth begins with that release. Confirm restart counts stop increasing before closing the incident.

retrieved.title: Application secret rotation
retrieved.heading: Rotation checks
retrieved.text:
Application secret rotation / Rotation checks
Rotate the Northstar application secret using the secret manager workflow. Create a new secret version and deploy consumers that can read it before disabling the previous version. Never put secret values in Git, logs or tickets.

Confirm the new version is mounted on every consumer replica. Use secret version identifiers in the rollout checklist and a synthetic authentication check to verify the change. Retain the old version during the approved overlap window of thirty minutes.

After the overlap window, revoke the old secret and verify that clients still authenticate. If any consumer fails, pause revocation and contact the secret owner. Record only version IDs and timestamps in the incident notes.
